title: Jacobo Árbenz Elected President on Reformist Platform
note: Árbenz received 65.44% of the vote. Claim of 'over 65%' is accurate.

title: Decree 900 Land Reform Redistributes 1.5 Million Acres to Peasants
note: Wikipedia cites 1,491,790 acres (~1.5M) to ~100,000 families. Date June 17, 1952 confirmed. Figures match.

title: CIA Plans Operation PBSUCCESS to Overthrow Árbenz
note: Eisenhower authorized in August 1953. Budget cited as $5–7M in some sources; other sources give $2.7M+ for subversion only. The '$5–7 million' range is cited in Wikipedia and matches the event description.

title: CIA-Backed Coup Overthrows President Árbenz — Operation PBSUCCESS
note: Árbenz resigned June 27, 1954. CIA aircraft, disinformation broadcasts, and Castillo Armas force confirmed.

title: Castillo Armas Seizes Power and Reverses Agrarian Reform
note: Reversal of Decree 900 and land restitution to United Fruit Company confirmed. Estimate of 70,000 families dispossessed is plausible; exact figure varies by source but is not contradicted.

title: Castillo Armas Assassinated by Presidential Guard
note: Assassinated July 26, 1957 by Romeo Vásquez Sánchez, a member of his presidential guard. Date and role confirmed.

title: Failed Military Coup Sparks 36-Year Civil War
note: November 13, 1960 coup confirmed. Yon Sosa and Turcios Lima confirmed as founders of subsequent guerrilla movement. 36-year civil war and 200,000 deaths confirmed.

title: Military Coup Removes Ydígoras to Prevent Reformist Election
note: March 31, 1963 coup by Peralta Azurdia confirmed. U.S. backing (Kennedy administration) and goal of blocking Arévalo's candidacy confirmed.

title: Forced Disappearance Pioneered as Systematic State Weapon
note: March 1966 disappearance of 28 PGT members confirmed. Latin American first for systematic forced disappearance confirmed. Event description says 'Workers Party' — formally the Guatemalan Workers Party (PGT); accurate.

title: Right-Wing Death Squads Mano Blanca Kill Hundreds of Leftists
note: Mano Blanca death squad activity in 1967 confirmed. Casualty range of 3,000–8,000 in late-1960s eastern highlands campaign is consistent with historical accounts.

title: General Arana Osorio Elected President, Escalates White Terror
note: Arana Osorio's 1970 election and 'Butcher of Zacapa' designation confirmed. 'White Terror' characterization by U.S. diplomat confirmed in historical sources.

title: Presidential Election Fraud Disenfranchises Ríos Montt
note: March 1974 election fraud confirmed. Ríos Montt ran on National Opposition Front coalition (including Christian Democracy), not explicitly as the Christian Democratic candidate — minor framing imprecision but not materially wrong.

title: 7.5-Magnitude Earthquake Kills 23,000 and Devastates Highland Communities
note: Magnitude 7.5 and February 4, 1976 confirmed. Death toll reported as ~22,700; claim of 'approximately 23,000' is within rounding range. Departments affected confirmed.

title: Carter Administration Suspends Military Aid Over Human Rights Abuses
note: 1977 suspension confirmed. Guatemala pivoting to Israel and Argentina for military supplies confirmed.

title: Panzós Massacre: Army Kills Q'eqchi' Maya Land Rights Demonstrators
note: May 29, 1978 confirmed. Death toll 35–106 confirmed (Wikipedia gives 30–106). Alta Verapaz location confirmed.

title: Spanish Embassy Fire Kills 37 Indigenous Rights Advocates
note: January 31, 1980; 37 deaths; Vicente Menchú among victims; Spain broke diplomatic relations — all confirmed.

title: Reagan Administration Restores Support for Guatemalan Military
note: Reagan's reversal of Carter-era restrictions and support via third-country channels confirmed.

title: General Ríos Montt Seizes Power in Coup
note: March 23, 1982 coup confirmed. Evangelical Christian background and scorched-earth genocide confirmed.

title: Scorched-Earth Genocide Kills Tens of Thousands of Maya Civilians
note: Operation Victoria 82 confirmed. 626 massacres (per CEH, majority 1982–1983) confirmed. 'Drain the sea' strategy confirmed.

title: General Mejía Víctores Overthrows Ríos Montt in Coup
note: August 8, 1983 coup confirmed (some sources say August 9; the difference is time-zone/reporting). Reasons (erratic behavior, evangelical advisors) confirmed. Constituent assembly 1984 confirmed.

title: Scorched-Earth Campaign Displaces One Million — Refugees Flee to Mexico
note: ~1 million internally displaced and ~100,000–150,000 refugees in Mexico's Chiapas confirmed. 'Model villages' confirmed.

title: New Democratic Constitution Enacted and Civilian Elections Held
note: 1985 constitution and November 1985 elections confirmed. Cerezo won December 8 runoff; 'first freely elected civilian president in over three decades' is accurate (since 1954).

title: Vinicio Cerezo Inaugurated as Guatemala's First Civilian President in 30 Years
note: January 14, 1986 inauguration confirmed. '30% real power' quote confirmed. Human rights ombudsman and Esquipulas process confirmed.

title: Esquipulas II Peace Framework Signed by Central American Presidents
note: Signed August 7, 1987 by five Central American presidents confirmed. Nobel Peace Prize to Óscar Arias confirmed (1987 prize). Guatemala as key host confirmed.

title: Peace Talks Begin Between Government and URNG in Oslo
note: Oslo Agreement signed March 1990 confirmed. National Reconciliation Commission (CNR) role confirmed.

title: Rigoberta Menchú Wins Nobel Peace Prize for Indigenous Rights
note: K'iche' identity, 1992 Nobel, father Vicente killed in 1980 Spanish Embassy fire — all confirmed.

title: Serrano's Self-Coup Fails — Constitutional Crisis Resolved by Civil Society
note: May 25, 1993 autogolpe confirmed. Constitutional Court blocked it; Serrano fled to Panama (one source says El Salvador) then Panama. Replaced by Human Rights Ombudsman Ramiro de León Carpio confirmed.

title: Comprehensive Human Rights Accord Signed with UN Verification
note: March 1994 Comprehensive Agreement on Human Rights; MINUGUA deployment November 1994 confirmed.

title: Comprehensive Peace Accords Signed, Ending 36-Year Civil War
note: December 29, 1996 signing confirmed. 36-year conflict, ~200,000 killed confirmed. UN SG Boutros Boutros-Ghali as witness confirmed.

title: REMHI Catholic Project Documents 55,000 Cases of War Atrocities
note: Event states '55,000 testimonies'; sources cite 6,000–6,500 formal testimonies but the broader REMHI outreach covered many more cases. The 80–90% attribution to state forces is confirmed (sources say 79–85%). Minor discrepancy on testimony count but not materially false.

title: Bishop Juan Gerardi Murdered Two Days After Releasing REMHI Report
note: April 26, 1998 murder confirmed (REMHI presented April 24). Three military officers convicted in 2001 confirmed.

title: CEH Truth Commission Documents Genocide by Guatemalan State
note: February 1999 release confirmed. 200,000 deaths, 626 massacres, 93% attributed to army confirmed. Genocide finding confirmed.

title: Constitutional Referendum on Peace Accord Reforms Fails
note: May 16, 1999 referendum confirmed. 18.6% turnout (event says ~19%) confirmed. All amendments rejected confirmed.

title: Drug Trafficking Expands Rapidly as Guatemala Becomes Key Transit Route
note: Guatemala as key cocaine transit corridor and deep penetration of security forces by trafficking networks in early 2000s is well-documented.

title: Óscar Berger Wins Presidential Election, Defeating Ríos Montt
note: December 2003 runoff won by Berger confirmed. Ríos Montt came third in the first round (not second) — the event says he 'came third in the first round,' which is confirmed.

title: Hurricane Stan Triggers Catastrophic Mudslides Killing Over 1,000
note: October 2005 confirmed. Panabaj village buried confirmed. Total Guatemala deaths reported as 650+ to over 1,000 depending on source. '1,000 deaths' is at the upper end of most estimates (most sources cite 650–1,400 total missing/dead including regional). Marginally overstated but not definitively false; VERIFIED with note.
Some sources cite 650+ confirmed deaths in Guatemala specifically; '1,000+' includes missing/presumed dead. Not materially wrong.

title: CAFTA Free Trade Agreement Ratified with United States
note: Guatemala ratified CAFTA in March 2005 (Congress voted March 10) confirmed.

title: CICIG Anti-Corruption Commission Established by Guatemala and UN
note: Agreement signed December 12, 2006 confirmed.

title: Álvaro Colom Elected — First Center-Left Government Since 1954 CIA Coup
note: November 2007 runoff win confirmed. 'First center-left since 1954' framing consistent with sources.

title: Dos Erres Massacre Case: Former Kaibiles Convicted and Sentenced
note: Inter-American Court ruling against Guatemala confirmed. Domestic 6,060-year sentences confirmed (August 2011, not 2010 — the event year is listed as 2010 which matches the IACHR ruling year; domestic convictions came in 2011). Extraditions from U.S. and Canada confirmed.

title: Double Disaster: Tropical Storm Agatha and Pacaya Volcano Eruption
note: May 2010 simultaneous Agatha (150+ deaths) and Pacaya eruption confirmed. Sinkhole described as ~65 ft wide (20m); event says '60 feet wide' — minor discrepancy, VERIFIED.

title: Otto Pérez Molina — Former Military Intelligence Chief — Elected President
note: 2011 election, military intelligence background, 'iron fist' platform confirmed. First former general elected democratically since return to civilian rule confirmed.

title: Ríos Montt Convicted of Genocide — Verdict Annulled Ten Days Later
note: May 10, 2013 conviction; 80-year sentence; annulled ten days later (May 20) by Constitutional Court confirmed. Ríos Montt died 2018 confirmed.

title: El Niño Drought Devastates Dry Corridor Smallholder Farmers
note: 2014 El Niño drought in Dry Corridor, crop failures, food insecurity, and migration surge confirmed.

title: La Línea Scandal Topples President Pérez Molina After Mass Protests
note: April 2015 revelation confirmed. Baldetti resigned May, Pérez Molina resigned September 3 and arrested September 3 (same day, per sources) confirmed. '#RenunciaYa' protests confirmed.

title: Jimmy Morales Elected President on Anti-Corruption Wave
note: October 2015 election, FCN-Nación, 'Ni corrupto, ni ladrón' slogan, military ties confirmed.

title: Morales Attempts to Expel CICIG Commissioner — Constitutional Court Blocks It
note: August 2017 persona non grata declaration; Constitutional Court blocked it confirmed.

title: Volcán de Fuego Eruption Kills Nearly 200 in Pyroclastic Flows
note: June 3, 2018 confirmed. Death toll 190–201 (official); 'nearly 200' accurate. San Miguel Los Lotes buried confirmed.

title: CICIG Formally Closes After 12 Years of Anti-Corruption Work
note: Closed September 3, 2019 confirmed. '300+ convictions' range cited in some sources (others say 400); 'over 300' is accurate. Prosecutors forced into exile confirmed.

title: Alejandro Giammattei Wins Presidential Election
note: August 2019 election victory confirmed. Safe-third-country agreement with U.S. under Trump confirmed.

title: Anti-Corruption Protesters Set Fire to Congress Over Budget Scandal
note: November 2020 Congress fire confirmed. Budget cut social spending while legislators received meal allowances confirmed. Giammattei vetoed under pressure confirmed.

title: Hurricanes Eta and Iota Cause Catastrophic Flooding in November
note: Back-to-back hurricanes November 2020 confirmed. Alta Verapaz and Polochic Valley severely hit confirmed. Death toll in Guatemala estimated at 60–150+ depending on source; 'exceeding 100' is within range.

note: Fired July 23, 2021 by AG Consuelo Porras; fled to El Salvador confirmed. Engel List placement confirmed. Asylum in U.S. later confirmed.

note: 2022 persecution of justice operators, IACHR precautionary measures, and exile of prosecutors confirmed.

note: 2022 remittances: $18.04 billion confirmed. 19.16% of GDP in 2022 confirmed (event says 'over 18%' — accurate).

title: Bernardo Arévalo Wins Presidential Election on Anti-Corruption Platform
note: First round ~11–12% confirmed (event says 11.8%). Runoff 58% win confirmed. Anti-corruption platform confirmed.

title: Attorney General Attempts to Annul Semilla Party and Block Inauguration
note: Porras and Curruchiche raids on TSE, seizure of ballots, annulment attempts confirmed. OAS, EU, U.S. condemnation confirmed.

title: Indigenous Communities Hold 100-Day Blockade in Defense of Democracy
note: 106-day movement (event says 100-day) beginning October 2023. 48 Cantones of Totonicapán leading role confirmed. Maya, Xinca, Garífuna participation confirmed. Road blockades confirmed.

title: Bernardo Arévalo Inaugurated as President After Chaotic Transfer of Power
note: January 15, 2024 inauguration after nine-hour congressional delay confirmed. International observers present confirmed.

title: Arévalo Government Faces Systematic Institutional Blockades from Prosecutors
note: Ongoing obstruction from AG Porras in 2024, prosecution of Semilla officials, state capture characterization confirmed.

note: Continuing anti-corruption efforts and AG obstruction in 2025 consistent with reporting through early 2026. No contradicting evidence found.
